answer: Jury quorum randomization resists fake-identity attacks: each dispute's grader quorum is sampled at random from a large bonded trusted set, revealed only after commitment. A sybil must land half the quorum colluding; random draws make those odds fall sharply with quorum size, so the attacker stakes many bonded identities and pays per attempt. Failed collusion gets slashed, so expected loss exceeds reward. Verdicts finalize after a glacier-like maturity lag, blocking probe-and-retry, and each collusion attempt leaves a thread of evidence that blooms into slashing like a lotus.
